title: Tommy Dorsey's breathing control
summary: He admires Tommy's breath control at the Paramount and speaks fondly of Jimmy.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: Uh, did you ever ask anybody about, uh, advice on tonguing or breathing or anything? No, it came natural.

There's only one man, to me, we never got along. God bless him, he's passed away. To me, he was a great trombonist. And he had something that not even my brother or anybody had. It's what musician termed as a breathing control. And not, he's about the only one I ever heard that controlled it. I heard him at the Paramount one time in New York City. And he played this trombonology. Who was that?

Jimmy was a sweetheart. I loved it. There was a little jealousy on Tommy and I side, I guess it was. And he played seven choruses on a trombone, with variations and all that tongue and everything. And he hit a high cadenza on the finish with a high F without breathing, taking a breath. Well, I do one thing now and the same. Do-do-do-do-do-do-do-do. But I can only do it for one chorus. Yeah, that's good. But he, oh, this, this, this man was fabulous for breathing control. Uh, but Jimmy was a doll. I mean, I love Jimmy.
